intro: To link to another slide in PowerPoint on Mac, select the text, shape or picture, then press ⌘K. In the dialog, choose This Document, pick the slide, click OK, and test the link in Slide Show.
tldr: Select the text, shape or picture you want to click.
Press ⌘K, or go to Insert > Link.
Choose This Document, open the slide list if it is closed, pick the slide and click OK.
Links only jump in Slide Show. In Normal view, right-click the link and choose Open Hyperlink to test it.
PowerPoint for Mac cannot link to a specific slide in a different file. Copy the slide into your deck first.

blocks.text: What a slide link does during a show

A slide link is a hyperlink whose target is another slide in the same file. The object you link becomes a clickable trigger while the show runs. Microsoft's hyperlink article uses the same steps for text, shapes and pictures, so the method does not change with the object.

PowerPoint bookmarks every slide automatically. That is why the slide list is ready inside the link dialog. You do not need to set up bookmarks before you link. Microsoft's bookmark article describes this behavior.
Finding the Link command on a Mac

On PowerPoint for Mac, the fastest route is ⌘K. The Link command also sits on the Insert menu, and it opens the same Insert Hyperlink dialog. Microsoft's shortcut list gives ⌘K for Insert a hyperlink, and Indezine's Mac list matches it. Indezine notes that its shortcuts assume a US English keyboard layout, so check the key on your own keyboard.
Choosing This Document and the target slide

The Insert Hyperlink dialog has a list of places on the left. Pick This Document for a link inside the same deck. Then find the slide list. In the bookmark article, Microsoft calls it Slide Titles, and you open it with the small chevron. Click the title of the slide you want, then click OK.

blocks.caption: The same option has different names. Use the one on your screen.

blocks.text: Expect the names to differ. Microsoft's pages do not always use the same label for the same option. Match the words on your screen to the table, and move on.
Test the link in Slide Show

A slide link does not jump while you edit. Start the show, click the linked item and watch the target slide appear. If the jump lands on the wrong slide, return to Normal view, select the same object, press ⌘K and pick the right target. The new target replaces the old one.

Microsoft's own test step happens in Normal view. Right-click the linked item and choose Open Hyperlink. That opens the target without starting the show, so you can check several links quickly. Use Slide Show for the final check, because it shows what the audience sees.
Why Link to this Slide may not show on right-click

Some people look for an option called 'Link to this Slide' on the right-click menu, and many cannot find it on Mac. A 2021 Microsoft Q&A thread shows the confusion. An MVP answer says the option does not exist, while a Microsoft support reply in the same thread says it exists in Microsoft 365 for Mac, with no menu path.
Do not spend time hunting for it. The Insert Hyperlink dialog is the path Microsoft documents. Its support article covers Microsoft 365 for Mac, PowerPoint 2024 for Mac and PowerPoint 2021 for Mac.
Make the link easy to spot

A link that looks like plain text is easy to miss in a show. Select the linked text, go to the Home tab, and open the Font Color arrow. Choose a color that stands out on your slide. Use the same color on every linked item, so the audience learns what to click.
Linking to a slide in a different file

This is the limit that trips people up. Microsoft says PowerPoint for macOS cannot link to a specific slide in another presentation. If the target lives in another file, copy the slide into your current deck first, then link to the copy.
A copied slide becomes part of your deck. Check its fonts, layout and images after the copy. The source file stays the same, so keep it as your backup.
Worked example: a contents slide with links

Say you have a contents slide at the start of a deck, with one line for each section. Build the contents slide first. Then select a line, press ⌘K, choose This Document, pick the first slide of that section and click OK. Repeat for each line.

Next, add a link back on each section slide that points to the contents slide. That gives your audience a way back without leaving the show. Run the show from the beginning and click every link once. If a link lands on the wrong slide, change only that link's target.
Mistakes that break slide links

items: Testing in Normal view and assuming the link is broken. Links only jump in Slide Show.
Selecting the whole text box when you meant one word. Select the words you want to click.
Deleting a target slide and leaving the link in place. Pick a new target for that link.
Assuming a link made on Windows needs a fix on Mac. Microsoft's Insider post says links created on any platform work on the others.

blocks.text: Update PowerPoint when links stop working

If links stop working after an update, update Office before you change the deck. Open any Office app and choose Help > Check for Updates. If Microsoft AutoUpdate opens, click Update or Update All, then relaunch the app. That update page is titled for work or school Macs, so a personal install may look slightly different.

The release notes list PowerPoint for Mac builds from September 16 to October 27, 2026. The newest build listed is 16.114.3, build 26102720. None of the notes mention hyperlinks or the Insert menu. Newer builds may exist, so check the release notes again if your version is newer.
Linking in PowerPoint for the web

If you also edit in a browser, the path is slightly different. Microsoft's Insider post describes Insert > Link > This Presentation, then a slide by number or title, then Insert. Links you create on any platform work on the others, so a link made on the Mac works in the web version.

On the web, the Insider post gives Ctrl+K for the slide link option on Windows. Microsoft's keyboard page lists ⌘K in the Mac column of its web table. Test the link in the browser before you present from it.
What to do after the links work

Once the links work, you will present the deck. Presenter View shows your notes and the next slide while the audience sees the current one. Read [how to use Presenter View in PowerPoint on Mac](/how-to/use-presenter-view-in-powerpoint) before the talk.

If the deck should run alone at a booth, read [how to loop a slide show in PowerPoint on Mac](/how-to/loop-a-slide-show-in-powerpoint). Then test the loop from start to finish, and check that your links still jump to the right slides.

faq.question: Can I link to a slide in a different PowerPoint file on Mac?
faq.answer: Not according to Microsoft. Its article says PowerPoint for macOS cannot link to a specific slide in another presentation. Copy the slide you need into the current deck, then link to the copy.

faq.question: Is there a Link to this Slide option on the right-click menu?
faq.answer: Sources conflict. An MVP in a 2021 Microsoft Q&A thread says the option does not exist. A Microsoft reply in the same thread says it exists in Microsoft 365 for Mac, without a menu path. Use Insert > Link or ⌘K instead.

faq.question: What is the keyboard shortcut to link to a slide on Mac?
faq.answer: Press ⌘K. Microsoft's shortcut list gives ⌘K for Insert a hyperlink, and Indezine's Mac list says the same. Indezine assumes a US English keyboard layout, so check the symbol if your layout is different.

faq.question: Why does the link work in Slide Show but not when I click it in Normal view?
faq.answer: Links only jump during the show. In Normal view, select the linked item, right-click it and choose Open Hyperlink to test it. That test step comes from Microsoft's article.

faq.question: Can I link a picture or a shape instead of text?
faq.answer: Yes. Microsoft's steps start with selecting the text, shape or picture. The same Insert > Link dialog applies to all three. A picture works well as a button on a contents slide.

faq.question: Do links made on Mac work in PowerPoint for the web?
faq.answer: Microsoft's Insider post says links created on any platform work on the others. On the web, the path is Insert > Link > This Presentation, according to the same post.

faq.question: Which PowerPoint versions does Microsoft's article cover?
faq.answer: The article covers Microsoft 365 for Mac, PowerPoint 2024 for Mac and PowerPoint 2021 for Mac. If your menus use different names, match the names on your screen to the steps above.

task: Link text or an object to another slide in the same deck
appliesTo: PowerPoint for Mac in Microsoft 365, PowerPoint 2024 and PowerPoint 2021
requirements: PowerPoint for Mac in Microsoft 365, PowerPoint 2024 or PowerPoint 2021
The target slide in the same presentation
A word, shape or picture to use as the link
Slide Show to test the jump

steps.name: Open the deck in Normal view
steps.text: Open the presentation in PowerPoint for Mac. Go to the slide that holds the text, shape or picture you want to use as the link. Stay in Normal view, which is where you edit. You will test the link in Slide Show later.
steps.tip: Slide links do not jump while you edit, so save the test for later.

steps.name: Select the words, shape or picture
steps.text: Highlight the words you want to click. For a shape or picture, click the object once so its handles appear. Do not select the whole text box unless the whole box should be the link.
steps.tip: If the Link option is greyed out, see the troubleshooting section for a text box workaround.

steps.name: Open the Insert Hyperlink dialog
steps.text: Go to the Insert menu and choose Link. Or press ⌘K while the same selection is still active. Either way, the Insert Hyperlink dialog opens.
steps.tip: Both routes open the same dialog, so use whichever you remember.

steps.name: Choose This Document
steps.text: In the list on the left of the dialog, click This Document. The dialog now shows the slides in the current presentation.
steps.tip: Microsoft's article calls this option Place in This Document. It is the same option.

steps.name: Expand the slide list
steps.text: Look for the slide titles section in the dialog. If the list is closed, click the chevron to open it. Microsoft's bookmark article uses the name Slide Titles for this list.
steps.tip: The bookmark article does not label its steps by platform, so match the names to what you see on screen.

steps.name: Pick the target slide
steps.text: Click the title of the slide you want the link to open. PowerPoint bookmarks every slide automatically, so the target is ready to use. You do not add a bookmark first.
steps.tip: If two slides look alike in the list, give the target slide a clear title first.

steps.name: Click OK to set the link
steps.text: Click OK. The link is set on the text, shape or picture you selected. Nothing jumps yet, because the real test happens in Slide Show.
steps.tip: Click the same object again later to see or change its link.

steps.name: Start the slide show
steps.text: Open the Slide Show tab and start the show from the beginning, or from the slide that holds the link. Links only work during the show, so this is the real test.
steps.tip: Start from the linked slide to save time when you check one link.

steps.name: Click the linked item
steps.text: Click the linked item while the show runs. PowerPoint should jump to the target slide. Use the arrow keys to move on from there.
steps.tip: If nothing happens, check the troubleshooting section for the common causes.

steps.name: Test in Normal view if you prefer
steps.text: To check a link without starting the show, go back to Normal view. Right-click the linked item and choose Open Hyperlink. Microsoft lists this as its test step for links.
steps.tip: Use Slide Show for the final check, because it shows what the audience sees.

shortcuts.action: Insert a hyperlink (opens the Insert Hyperlink dialog)

troubleshooting.problem: The Link option is greyed out
troubleshooting.fix: Microsoft's Insider post says that if the Link option is disabled, you can put the selected text in a separate text box and try again. That post is about PowerPoint for the web, so treat it as a workaround to test on your Mac.

troubleshooting.problem: The target slide is missing from the list
troubleshooting.fix: Check that the slide still exists in this deck. If you deleted it, the link has no target. Pick a new slide in the dialog and click OK to replace the link.

troubleshooting.problem: Clicking the link does nothing in Normal view
troubleshooting.fix: That is expected. Links only jump in Slide Show. Start the show to test, or right-click the link and choose Open Hyperlink.

troubleshooting.problem: Links fail after an update or on an older build
troubleshooting.fix: Open any Office app and choose Help > Check for Updates. If Microsoft AutoUpdate opens, click Update or Update All, then relaunch PowerPoint. The latest Mac release notes list no hyperlink changes.

troubleshooting.problem: You need a link to a slide in another file
troubleshooting.fix: Microsoft says PowerPoint for Mac cannot link to a specific slide in another presentation. Copy the slide you need into the current deck, then link to the copy.
